startup.name: CharacterQuilt
startup.one_liner: Computer use agents to deploy enterprise marketing campaigns
startup.description: CharacterQuilt builds computer use agents that deploy enterprise marketing campaigns. Customers send a brief as they would to an agency, and the agents build segments, create on brand creative and deploy the campaign inside tools such as HubSpot, Marketo, Pardot, WordPress and LinkedIn. It replaces agency ops work that takes weeks. Four people in San Francisco with named early customers (1upHealth, ABC Fitness, Emplifi) per its description. Revenue is likely per campaign or subscription.

yc_acceptance.basis: Starting rate about 1 percent (YC investor line, third party range 0.6 to 2 percent). Test setup: already accepted, reference only. Up for named customers, a painful agency cost problem and a team of 4. Down for a crowded AI marketing field and reliance on computer use agents that frontier labs also build. Net about 6 percent as a plain applicant.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC would most plausibly question durability: computer use agents that click through marketing tools are exactly what the model labs and the marketing platforms are building, and the customers named are small or mid sized. The reviewer would want evidence that customers pay and renew rather than run pilots, and that the brand memory is more than a prompt.

ladder.why_it_fails: The seed fails to clear 500K if investors read the product as a thin wrapper on computer use models that labs improve every quarter, or as an agency in disguise where humans still check each campaign. Four people and a few small logos are early. Autotab, an earlier computer use agent startup, did not raise beyond a small amount, and many AI agent teams in the YC cohort stay at pre-seed.

ladder.why_it_fails: A Series B requires moving from campaign deployment to a platform marketing leaders standardize on. HubSpot, Salesforce and Adobe can add agent features and distribute them at no marginal cost, and agency relationships are sticky. ladder.why_it_fails: A Series C needs a large enterprise software business. Few marketing automation companies reached that size, and the market is dominated by incumbents. Only strong net retention and a larger platform scope would get CharacterQuilt there; otherwise acquisition by a marketing cloud is the likely end.

outcomes.why_it_fails: Most likely the company stays a small agency like service because campaign deployment varies per customer and agents need human supervision, or marketing platforms and frontier labs ship the same agents natively. Past marketing tooling in YC such as Marketfox did not survive among funded rivals, and acquisition by a marketing platform for under 100M is the common soft landing.

killers.risk: Model labs and marketing platforms ship computer use and campaign agents natively
killers.evidence: Computer use is a generic capability frontier labs ship, and HubSpot and Salesforce control the APIs the agents depend on.
killers.mitigation: Own the brand memory and cross tool workflow rather than the clicking.

killers.risk: Agents are unreliable and need human checking, so margins look like an agency
killers.evidence: Enterprise campaigns have approvals and brand rules, and mistakes in live campaigns are costly.
killers.mitigation: Start with low risk deployment tasks and show error rates.

killers.risk: Long enterprise sales cycles and pilots that never convert
killers.evidence: Treble.ai needed years of customer growth before an A, and enterprise marketing buyers are slow and risk averse.
killers.mitigation: Sell to mid market teams with an owner who feels the ops pain.

killers.risk: Agencies and tools resist or lock out agents, with API changes and terms of service
killers.evidence: Agents depend on logins and interfaces of third party tools that can block automation.
killers.mitigation: Build official integrations and become a partner.

technical_complexity.rationale: Computer use agents that operate Pardot, Marketo and LinkedIn reliably are hard: interfaces change, sessions need credentials and errors are costly. A small team can build a demo in three months but not production reliability. Brand learning from past campaigns adds a data and evaluation problem.

who: Frontier AI labs with computer use agents
takeover_risk.rationale: Marketing platforms have the data, distribution and incentive to add agentic campaign building within a year. Labs improve computer use every release. Past examples show that point tools in marketing tend to be absorbed or stay small.

evidence.claim: Enterprise marketing teams pay agencies large fees to configure campaigns in their own tools, per the company's own description.

brand.name: CharacterQuilt
brand.name_check: python3 -I scripts/name_features.py --score "CharacterQuilt" --era 2022+: 14 characters, 4 syllables, kind compound_words.
strengths: Short form CQ is easy to use
weaknesses: Long and gives no hint of marketing
brand.rationale: A distinctive compound name is ownable, like past YC names that were invented words, but at 14 characters it is long and unrelated to marketing, so buyers rely on the CQ short form. The effect on success is small and neutral.

narrative.headline: An early but concrete bet on agents for marketing ops; a seed is likely, but platform and lab risk weighs on later rounds.
narrative.general_summary: CharacterQuilt automates the ops work of marketing campaigns, a painful job that agencies charge large fees for, and already names several customers. That makes a seed above 500K likely. The risk is structural: computer use agents are a generic capability that labs improve and that marketing platforms can bundle, and enterprise sales are slow. The closest YC analogs, Hightouch and Treble.ai, reached later rounds only after widening scope or reaching many customers, while narrower marketing tools stalled. We set the seed above the cohort anchor and the later steps near it.

assumptions: Seed means a round above about 500K within about 12 months of the batch start.
Customer names come from the company's own description and are unverified.
Base rates are B2B 2022 to 2025; recent batches are right censored.
Competition and platform claims rest on general market knowledge, not company specific data.
